_doc: library/status_3.json (workstream bt-web, 2026-11-13). Status per source acquired from the hosts that became reachable on 2026-11-13; status.json and status_2.json are not edited. Statuses: ingested, partial, blocked, unusable. Each task merges its own entries (task field); ingested here means the file or text is acquired and hash-recorded, not that every claim was mined.

sources.reason: 436 files, sha256 in images_ledger.json, every file decoded
191 records, caption and notes read for camera-position statements
2 of 430 resources fetched as masters (25 to 130 MB each)
23 comparisons parsed verbatim; images identified against LOC records by feature matching
captions of plates 3 to 8 read; plates are photocopies and were not matched
62 records of the wide search (outside the cwp collection): 57 medium JPEGs with sha256, 5 records not digitized by the Library, each read and classified
34 NPS place pages read for camera places
36 figure captions cut verbatim from the saved text; images matched against the catalogue; 22 ties confirmed by looking

resolved 2026-11-14: it is LOC record 2018671576 (resource cwpb.00084, a stereo negative, caption from the negative sleeve: Gettysburg from the Cemetery. July 1863); the record carries the call number LC-B815- 273 [P&P]

reachable, but a plain request to any address of the catalog (and to its api/v2 path) returns the same 5 KB single-page-application shell, not data; the catalog API needs a key (an account, an owner act); a browser read was not made. No NARA description of a Gettysburg photograph was read

records of the wide search that the Library has not digitized (its search result carries the placeholder 500x500_notdigitized.png): 2024640246, 2024640258, 2025160363, 2025160541, 2025160547; each is listed in the registry with its title and the reason it has no frame to look at

the Library item holds the album pages as images (1024 px copies and 100 MB master TIFFs) without a text layer; at 1024 px the letterpress is too small for OCR and the masters were not fetched; the plate captions that LOC transcribed into its picture records are used (plates 35 and 39)
the search returned no records: there is no Project Gutenberg edition of the Sketch Book
